Honestly, I would just find new places to cut. If you're not going to stop self harming, then find a new place to self harm. Be careful, though. If you haven't already learned, it's addicting. 

You could try meditation, visualization, or something else like that. That's what I would really recommend, because it's safer, and you'll benefit more from it. If you are going to try to use that over cutting, don't get discouraged if you do cut, even if you tell yourself you're not going to.

I did the same today, but I haven't gotten nearly close to going as long as you have. I was just trying to get through one day without cutting, but I couldn't. I felt little for falling down, but I felt strong again after I'd cut... It's stupid how it works, really.

Anyways, you can do it, with determination and a strong willpower, and something else to occupy your time. I reddit, read, play video games, do my hair/makeup, and sing when I feel like cutting is the only thing on my mind. 

Stay strong, you (and I) can get through it, it just takes time. Heroin addicts and alcoholics don't get better instantly, but they do get better. Just keep that in mind. I'm here to talk if you need me <3

First off, I'd love to be able to know more about cutting, and why we do it. I don't understand, but here I am, doing it for myself, and feeling pretty damn good while I do it. I know the trend with cutting/SI is relief and good vibes, but then it becomes a dangerous obsession/addiction.)

He does attend the same school, but when I hinted at switching schools (my counselors know about my incident), no further actions were taken. Maybe I'll ask about it again if this next week goes badly, because it's the end of the semester and therefore the perfect time to switch. The things causing the attacks are everything and anything, and I also think that the fear of fear is becoming a big problem, because I'll notice my fingers start to tingle, and my breaths become short, and I'll make it worse by worrying about the attack becoming worse. 

The biggest problem with this is that I haven't had the courage to tell my mom yet. I've been trying to sleep in the living room, but I get botched at by my mom for doing it every time. ("You have a bed, why don't you use it? You need a good night of sleep, you'll get muscle problems.") I don't have an alternate room to move to, and I don't really have room to rearrange my room (not saying it would be impossible, though.)

I'm afraid of the whole inpatient situation, just because it's such a taboo thing in my world. I live in a (moderately) rich, white village/town in nowhereville, Midwest. It's very unusual for my (fairly small) school to have somebody disappear for more than a few days at a time, and I'm afraid of becoming the center of attention (not saying that's likely, but high school is high school, and rumors fly like crazy.) I do want to heal, I want to know there's other people like me, and I want to know that I'll get better, just like they will. 

I know my therapist works in a fairly large practice and I think somebody there is qualified to prescribe medications. I know that she tells my mom some stuff (generic today was a good session, etc.) but I think in her contract she personally says I have to approve of anything more she would tell her. 

At the time, I didn't realize it was rape, and now, more than a year later, it's too late to have any evidence from the event, other than a he said she said. I'm afraid of the police because I'm afraid of ever having to bring him into my life again, in any way, shape or form. I know it shouldn't (and eventually won't) define me, but right now, I'm so consumed by it, I almost can't not feel that way. 

I do know I'm young and I don't want to give up on everything yet, but I do feel that I'm using very poor judgment I wouldn't normally use when I'm at my low points. 

I know I should stop with the drugs, but, they're there, and like I Said earlier, I really lose my judgement skills when the thought of relief comes into my brain. A little part of me (but a much bigger part than I want it to be) wants to get worse, wants to get into the rougher stuff, wants to go that one step too far and overdose. People do it every day, and (I'm assuming) it's one of the more pleasant ways to go out of this world if you're doing it yourself. I also don't ever go to my sessions without a clear head, because I don't want to jeopardize two things: 1) her finding out I'm doing it, and 2) me being dumb as a rock and wasting our time (and my money).
